capture.final_message:
Treat each side of both equivalences as an independently true standard fact, then assemble the `And` and the two `Iff`s.

- For fixed points, use set extensionality: an element is globally fixed exactly when it is fixed by every `m : M`, which is precisely membership in `⋂ m, fixedBy M m`.

- Represent `MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient.orbit x` as the fiber of the quotient map over `x`. If `φ` is a right inverse, then `φ x` represents `x`; equality in the orbit quotient is equivalent to lying in the same group orbit. This identifies that fiber with `orbit G (φ x)`.

- Every quotient class has a representative. Prove nonemptiness of its fiber by quotient induction, using the representative itself.

- For orbit stability under a monoid element, write any orbit point as `n • a`. Then
  `m • (n • a) = (m * n) • a`,
  so the image remains in the same orbit.

The group assumption is essential only for identifying quotient fibers with full orbits; forward invariance of an orbit needs merely a monoid action.
